newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DALLAS BEATS VANCOUVER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DALLAS BEATS VANCOUVER.

text.p: Jere Lehtinen had the go-ahead goal and an assist as the Dallas Stars extended their unbeaten streak to nine games and damaged Vancover's playoff chances with a 3-2 victory over the Canucks on Sunday.

Former Canuck Greg Adams added an insurance tally in the third period for the Stars, who are 7-0-2 since March 1st, their longest unbeaten streak since they went a franchise-record 12 games without a loss in 1981-82.
Dallas is 20-6-3 since the All-Star break and leads second-place Detroit by nine points in the Central Division.
Trevor Linden and David Roberts scored for Vancouver.
At New Jersey, Bill Guerin and Scott Stevens scored in a 44-second span of the first period as the New Jersey Devils coasted to a 5-2 victory over the Los Angeles Kings.
Guerin scored two of New Jersey's four first-period goals, and Scott Stevens had a goal and two assists. The Devils improved to 7-2-1 in their last 10 games.
Mike Dunham made 22 saves for the Devils, whose 46 points since the All-Star break are tops in the conference.
Kevin Stevens and Glen Murray scored for Los Angeles.

In Chicago, Ulf Dahlen scored his first goal in six weeks with 16:02 left in the third period, giving the Chicago Blackhawks a 3-2 victory over the Buffalo Sabres, who lost their fourth straight game.
Jeff Hackett made 25 saves for Chicago.
Donald Audette and Richard Smehlik scored for the Sabres.
In Detroit, Steve Rucchin scored off a rebound at 3:41 of overtime, and Mikhail Shtalenkov recorded his second shutout of the season as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim blanked the Red Wings, 1-0.

"I thought we had our legs tonight and it surprised me," said Anaheim coach Ron Wilson. "We pressured the puck well, all over the place, and did a great job getting in front of them and making them take some indirect routes."
Mike Vernon finished with 30 saves for Detroit, which had its eight-game home unbeaten streak snapped.
"He kept is in the game," Red Wings coach Scotty Bowman said of his goalie. "I thought they had better chances than we did."

In St Louis, Joe Murphy's goal early in the third period put St. Louis ahead and Grant Fuhr made it stand up as the Blues improved their playoffs chances with a 3-2 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers.

Philadelphia defenceman Petr Svoboda coughed the puck up in his own zone and Murphy sent a wrist shot from the inside edge of the right faceoff circle under sliding goaltender Ron Hextall with 17:17 remaining to break a 2-2 tie.
Craig MacTavish won three faceoffs down the stretch to preserve the win.
